hero.title: Before changing HR work, organize the workflow first
hero.subtitle: If attendance, payroll, contracts, and advisory records remain scattered, adding AI only creates another tool. HR AX starts from the ERP and document formats you already use, selects repeatable workflows, and connects them to reviewable automation.

pain.title: HR operations need structure before AI adoption
pain.subtitle: When ERP, spreadsheets, messengers, and document templates each move separately, automation impact stays limited. HR AX first organizes high-frequency and high-risk work.

items.label: Scattered
items.title: Records exist, but context is broken
items.description: Attendance, payroll, contracts, and advisory logs are managed separately, forcing teams to re-check them during handovers or audits.

items.label: Manual
items.title: Document work remains repetitive
items.description: Hiring, resignation, leave, and contract changes still require teams to compare forms and fields every time.

items.label: Risk
items.title: Review evidence is not retained
items.description: Even with AI-assisted answers, labor risk does not decrease unless the approval basis and reviewer are recorded.

modules.title: Start HR AX with consultable units of work
modules.subtitle: More important than a general chatbot is the work queue, documents, approvals, and reporting flow that HR teams handle every day.

items.title: Document and form automation
items.description: Draft contracts, certificates, work rules, and notices using existing templates and ERP fields.

items.title: Labor advisory support
items.description: Create reviewable draft answers from advisory history and internal standards.

items.title: Joiner, leaver, and leave workflows
items.description: Operate hiring, resignation, leave, disciplinary, and training work by owner, due date, and approval status.

items.title: Risk reporting
items.description: Turn attendance, payroll, contract, and safety data into monthly reports and executive summaries.

architecture.title: Add a reviewable execution layer without replacing the existing ERP
architecture.subtitle: Define the connection scope around the FAIR CRM/ERP, spreadsheets, and document templates already in operation, then expand step by step.

layers.title: Work data cleanup
layers.description: Standardize attendance, payroll, contract, and advisory fields and identify connectable sources.

layers.title: Process orchestration
layers.description: Design request intake, owner assignment, review, approval, and record storage as one flow.

layers.title: Governed AI use
layers.description: Use AI results with permissions, audit logs, source documents, and expert approval built in.

workflow.title: Validate small, then expand from diagnosis to pilot
workflow.subtitle: Like the reference sites, the page makes the diagnosis, prototype, and operational adoption path clear while adding the review responsibility required in HR and labor work.

steps.title: Workflow diagnosis
steps.description: Select HR work with high repetition and risk through interviews and source materials.

steps.title: Data and form mapping
steps.description: Organize ERP fields, spreadsheets, document templates, and approval standards into connectable structures.
steps.output: Output: field map and screen draft

steps.title: Prototype
steps.description: Build work queues, document drafts, and review screens as real screens and collect feedback.

steps.title: Adoption and expansion
steps.description: Expand scope using owner training and operating logs as the basis.
steps.output: Output: operating rules and improvement roadmap

cta.title: Can AX be applied to our HR operations?
cta.subtitle: Using your current ERP, spreadsheets, and document templates, we identify the application points with fast impact and low risk.
